name: Regular tests can protect women from cervical cancer

content.text: According to the World Health Organization, 30 per cent of cancers can be prevented through early detection. In the case of cervical cancer, early screening through a gynaecological examination - a pap smear - can be vital, according to Dr Aliya Aziz, Consultant Gynaecologist and Obstetrician at Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH). Pap smear is a test that detects changes in the neck of the womb that may lead to cancer. "An initial pap smear should be performed once a girl turns 21 or within three years of marriage. Thereafter, it may be done once in two to three years or annually as advised by your doctor," said Dr Aziz. She also talked about reducing the risk of gynaecological cancers by adopting a healthier diet rich in fruits and vegetables, and keeping fit.

Speaking about cancer in children, Dr Zehra Fadoo, Consultant Paediatric Haematologist and Oncologist, AKUH, said, "We do not have numbers from Pakistan, but rough estimates show that nearly 8,000 to 10,000 children are diagnosed with cancer each year." Fortunately, improved medication and research means that children have a better chance of surviving cancer, if detected early on, than they did a few decades ago. Dr Fadoo added that in developed countries, childhood cancers have been managed so well that in most cases, children have been 'cured' or gone into long-term remission. Similar measures can be implemented in Pakistan also.

Other common cancers include those of the head and neck, which are commonly seen in the cells that line the inside of the nose, mouth and throat. Dr Mubasher Ikram, Consultant ENT Surgeon, AKUH, explained that less common head and neck cancers include salivary gland tumours, lymphomas and sarcomas, which cover nearly 10 per cent of cancers in the body. He said that such types of cancers are more common in men, and Karachi has the highest incidence of them. The choice of treatment depends on the size of the tumour, its location, and whether it has spread to other parts of the body. Commonly used treatments for managing head and neck cancer are radiation therapy, surgery and chemotherapy.

Although the exact cause for these cancers is unknown, tobacco is regarded as the single greatest risk factor, with 75 to 80 per cent of the oral and throat cancers occurring primarily among smokers. Other intoxicants like alcohol also raise the risk of oral cancer. "People who smoke along with using other substances are nearly 15 times at higher risk of oral cancer than those who use only one of the two substances," said Dr Ikram. He added that other substances such as pan, chalia, gutka and naswar are also highly risky.

Further stressing the harms of tobacco use, Professor Javaid Khan, Chair, National Alliance for Tobacco Control and Consultant Pulmonologist, AKUH, said that tobacco damages nearly every organ in the human body and is linked to at least 15 different cancers, accounting for 40 per cent of all cancer deaths in Pakistan. He said that cigarette smoking alone causes 90 per cent of lung cancer deaths in the country. "Tobacco use is also responsible for most cancers of the voice box, mouth, food pipe and bladder," said Dr Khan, adding that people who smoke cigars are 10 times more likely to develop mouth and throat cancer compared to non-smokers.

Dr Khan also spoke about exposure to second-hand smoke as a risk factor for lung cancer. "In spite of a ban on smoking at public places, over 70 per cent of Pakistani children get exposed to second-hand smoke at hotels, restaurants, shopping centres and in public transport. Even fast food chains, which are completely smoke-free in other part"

content.author: Iqra Azmat
content.description: "Karachi, Pakistan: Three quarters of all cervical cancer cases occur in developing nations, primarily among younger women, yet awareness about this cancer is seriously lacking in these countries. On the occasion of World Cancer Day, doctors at Aga Khan University shared information about various cancers and spoke about their prevention and management.
